services.name: Whale Watching
services.desc: Whales are majestic creatures, and watching them live and swim in their natural habitat is an unforgettable experience. Labrador Fishing Charters is pleased to announce that we are now offering Massachusetts Whale Watching Tours. Our boat offers customers the opportunity to whale watch at eye level, unlike other whale watching boats that are 15’ above the bay. On those types of boats, it’s near impossible to get close to the action, and understand what life is really like for the whales. Customers have the opportunity to see a variety of whales when they trek out on the Massachusetts Bay with us, including humpback, finback and minke whales, and sometimes we even run into killer (orca)

blurb: Labrador Fishing Charters offers a variety of offshore and inshore fishing packages in Massachusetts Bay, including deep-sea fishing for tuna, striped bass, flounder, cod, porbeagle and thresher sharks. They welcome anglers of any level and age and provide family-friendly children's fishing trips that include fishing and lobster pot pulling. They also offer whale watching, bird watching, and lighthouse tours.

quotes.text: ★ ★ ★ ★ ★We were originally scheduled for Tuna and the night before, I got a text from captain Mike. He let us know that the Tuna/Haddock haven’t been great lately- he recommended we go after Striped Bass. It was a group of 6 of us…We had an Epic day. Epic! By the time we started sniping these bass, it was like we were all fishing together. You couldn’t possibly avoid how passionate these dudes were about fishing out there…Caught a bunch…Our group is already planning another charter. Dean Paul Reviewed in Spring 2022

★ ★ ★ ★ ★An amazing morning spent on the water! The crew is incredibly knowledgeable learned all about the islands but more importantly caught a ton of awesome fish!!! Could not recommend more! One of my favorite things we’ve done in Boston area. HUGE BONUS! The bathroom is the cleanest and nicest I’ve seen on a boat all around 5 star service. Emma Horgan Reviewed in Summer 2022
